7.0.0.en: In the accursed thing: in the forbidden things.

7.0.1.en: Achan: a name meaning troubling or disturbing.

7.0.2.en: Achan sinned against God by taking from the spoils of Jericho, from which God had commanded that no one should take, but that they be set apart for the house of the Lord. By his sin he stirred up the wrath of God against all the people, because Achan is a member of one body, so by his sin all the people sinned. In addition, the people were preoccupied with the victory and so were negligent in discovering Achan's theft of the spoils.

7.1.0.en: Ai: its meaning is a heap of stones, and it is a small city compared with Jericho, located east of Bethel (Map 2). Before attacking Ai, and without seeking the mind of God, Joshua sent men to discover its condition and fortifications, and they did as he asked. After Jericho Joshua began preparing to attack Ai because it was an entrance to the land of Canaan.

7.1.2.en: Mount Gerizim Bethel Gezer Ai Jarmuth Jerusalem Azekah Map (2)

7.2.0.en: The opinion of the spies when they returned to Joshua was that the city did not deserve the attack of all the people because of its smallness, but that two or three thousand men would suffice.

7.3.0.en: Shebarim: its meaning is stones, and it is located west of Ai; it is a slope between Ai and Jericho.

7.3.1.en: The heart of the people melted and became as water: they fell into great fear and weakness.

7.3.2.en: Joshua obeyed their advice, again without asking God His opinion, and the result was defeat and the death of thirty-six men of the people, and they pursued them down the slope on which the city was built, so the people were very afraid and terrified.

7.3.3.en: Be careful to take refuge in God in every great and small matter of your life, so that you learn humility and are reassured and protect yourself from every deviation.

7.4.0.en: Joshua and the leaders and elders of the people hurried to God and fasted and prayed with many supplications from morning until evening, and they humbled themselves before Him in prostration, and tore their clothes as a sign of their great grief, and put dust on their heads in humility and contrition before God.

7.5.0.en: The Amorites: tribes from the descendants of Canaan.

7.5.1.en: Joshua reproached God, who had permitted their crossing and dried up the river Jordan for them, as if God by this had delivered them to the inhabitants of the land so that they might destroy His people; indeed, in the weakness of his faith, he wished they had not crossed the Jordan and that it would have sufficed them to dwell east of it with the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh.

7.6.0.en: Joshua was deeply affected because the defeat of the people and their flight before their enemies would be heard of throughout the land, so that the inhabitants of Canaan would take courage and rise against the people of God and fight them and destroy them, and this would dishonor the name of God, as if the Lord had not been able to defend His people and so they perished.

7.6.1.en: Here Joshua appears as a spiritual leader who seeks the glory of God and the safety of his people.

7.7.0.en: The Lord had compassion on Joshua and commanded him to rise, and revealed to him the secret of the people's defeat before Ai, which was their offense against God by breaking their previous covenant to obey God and respect His commandments engraved on the tablets of the covenant. Their fall progressed from the offense to the transgression of the covenant by taking of the accursed things, then theft, denial and hiding among their stuff.

7.8.0.en: Accursed: falling under the curse of God because of the accursed thing in their midst.

7.8.1.en: The sin of the people was the cause of their defeat and of their not standing before the enemies, since they had become accursed like them, and God would not be with them unless they repented and removed the sin from their midst.

7.9.0.en: God asked Joshua to command the people to sanctify themselves, by bathing and washing their clothes and offering repentance before God, that is, washing their hearts; and He declares to them that the cause of their defeat before Ai is the presence of sin in their midst, and the accursed thing, that is, the sin, must be removed so that they may stand before the enemies.

7.10.2.en: Households: the families that dwell in this house.

7.10.3.en: Man by man: that is, every man with his family.

7.10.4.en: He also asked him that they should all come forward the next day to the tent of meeting, and the Lord would single out the guilty tribe, then the family within the tribe, then the guilty house, then the individual who committed the offense. This was done by means of the Urim and Thummim in the tent of meeting, which are two stones that the high priest carried, by which God declared His approval or refusal of anything, and the exposure of the guilty one may have been done by lot.

7.11.0.en: The guilty one must receive his punishment, which is burning with fire, he and what he stole and all that he has, for his transgression of the covenant of the Lord and his defiling of all the people.

7.11.1.en: A person falls into evil, and then his fall progresses until he becomes a slave to it and bound to it, and perishes. Blessed is he who examines himself first by first and saves himself from falling by repentance.

7.12.0.en: Joshua rose early the next day as was his habit, for he was an active man who hurries to carry out God's commands, and he did what God asked of him, and God determined that the guilty one was Achan of the tribe of Judah, and this was most likely done by lot. All this while Achan's conscience was not moved to offer repentance of his own accord and regret for the offense that caused the defeat and the death of thirty-six men. For sin will be exposed, even after a while, however much we hide it.

7.13.0.en: Joshua began a careful investigation with Achan and did not hasten to condemn him, but gave him an order to declare what he had done and not to hide any of it.

7.13.1.en: The following is noticed in Joshua's words with Achan:

7.13.2.en: 1- His concern that there should be a public trial so that no one would think that God had wronged him.

7.13.3.en: 2- Joshua's fatherliness and gentleness toward Achan, for he does not accuse him of anything before he confesses, although God had shown that he was a sinner, and so he addresses him, "My son."

7.13.4.en: 3- He declares to Achan that his confession is not only before Joshua but before God first; therefore he demanded of him, saying, "Give glory to God."

7.14.0.en: Achan admitted his offense in detail after God had exposed him and he was compelled to admit it.

7.15.0.en: Achan saw, then coveted, then took, then hid in the ground. Thus he progressed in the offense for the sake of a costly mantle, silver coins and a wedge of gold, which he held on to for himself, contrary to the Lord's command to burn everything except the metals that were to be delivered to the tent of meeting.

7.16.0.en: Joshua sent messengers to verify the confession, and they found the stolen things and brought them to him, and this was clear evidence of accusation proving Achan's crime.

7.17.0.en: Joshua took the stolen things with all of Achan's possessions and all those who had supported him in his offense and covered up for him, his sons and daughters, and brought them to the valley of Achor.

7.18.0.en: Here Joshua, the deliberate leader, issued his final judgment on Achan, who had troubled all the people and so deserved that the Lord should trouble him. He was stoned, killed and burned, as was done with the people of Jericho whose possessions he had taken, so that it became necessary to treat him as one of them.

7.18.1.en: God refused to have the gold and silver brought into His house like the rest of the spoils of Jericho, because these were stolen goods; they were connected with the sin of Achan, and God rejects everything connected with sin.

7.19.0.en: Unto this day: the day Joshua wrote this book.

7.19.1.en: The people made a great heap of stones over Achan so that it would remain as long as possible and remind them of the consequence of treachery. Here the anger of God turned away from His people, but Achan lost everything he had stolen, and all his material possessions, and his whole life.

7.19.2.en: To everything under the heavens there is a time, so do not seek to acquire it before that time as Achan did and lost everything, whereas if he had waited until the conquest of Ai he would have obtained all that he wanted of the spoils without any punishment. So do not be preoccupied with material things, because your God arranges them for you at the proper time.

7.19.3.en: Victory over Ai (1) A well-ordered plan (vv. 1-8:) 1 And the Lord said unto Joshua, Fear not, neither be thou dismayed: take all the people of war with thee, and arise, go up to Ai: see, I have given into thy hand the king of Ai, and his people, and his city, and his land: 2 And thou shalt do to Ai and her king as thou didst unto Jericho and her king: only the spoil thereof, and the cattle thereof, shall ye take for a prey unto yourselves: lay thee an ambush for the city behind it. 3 So Joshua arose, and all the people of war, to go up against Ai: and Joshua chose out thirty thousand mighty men of valour, and sent them away by night. 4 And he commanded them, saying, Behold, ye shall lie in wait against the city, even behind the city: go not very far from the city, but be ye all ready: 5 And I, and all the people that are with me, will approach unto the city: and it shall come to pass, when they come out against us, as at the first, that we will flee before them, 6 (For they will come out after us) till we have drawn them from the city; for they will say, They flee before us, as at the first: therefore we will flee before them. 7 Then ye shall rise up from the ambush, and seize upon the city: for the Lord your God will deliver it into your hand. 8 And it shall be, when ye have taken the city, that ye shall set the city on fire: according to the commandment of the Lord shall ye do. See, I have commanded you.

8.0.0.en: After the removal of the accursed thing, God reassured Joshua and asked him to take the whole army with him as he did when entering Jericho, and not to make light of the enemies as he made light of them in the first attack on Ai, and the Lord promised him victory over the city.

8.0.1.en: He commanded the going out of all the warriors, whose number was about six hundred thousand (Num 11:21), not that they should all fight, because he had chosen from them thirty thousand (v. 3) to fight Ai because of its smallness, but the going out of the whole army was for the following reasons:

8.0.2.en: 1- To encourage their brethren who would attack Ai.

8.0.3.en: 2- That they might see God's victory and so be encouraged in their fighting of the enemies in all the land of Canaan.

8.0.4.en: 3- That they might share in taking the spoils of the city of Ai.

8.0.5.en: And God says to Joshua, "I have given ... the king of Ai, and his people", in the past tense, for since God has commanded, His word will surely come to pass.

8.1.0.en: God announced to Joshua that he would triumph over Ai and possess it and kill its king as he did to Jericho. And God allowed him to let the people take the spoils of Ai. And He set for him a plan for the war, which was to make an ambush of men of war who would hide behind the city; this is a stratagem of war known from ancient times, and it shows the necessity that Joshua do everything in his power to conquer the city under God's guidance and not be idle, relying on God's giving him victory.

8.2.0.en: Lie in wait: hide without the people of Ai seeing you.

8.2.1.en: Joshua chose, by God's command, thirty thousand strong men of war, and commanded them to make an ambush, that is, to hide behind Ai and near it, and to be ready for war.

8.2.2.en: There are two opinions about the details of these war plans:

8.2.3.en: 1- The thirty thousand are those who fought Ai, and five thousand of them lie in wait behind the city from the previous night (v. 12), while the rest, who are twenty-five thousand, attack the city in the early morning with Joshua; and when Joshua commands the thirty thousand to make the ambush, he means that part of them will do this work.

8.2.4.en: 2- The second opinion is that thirty thousand made an ambush behind Ai made up of two parts, five thousand of them beside the city and twenty-five thousand behind Bethel, which is the helper and supporter of Ai (v. 17). As for the rest of the men of war among the children of Israel, whose number was six hundred thousand, they attacked the city in the morning under the leadership of Joshua himself.

8.3.0.en: Joshua completes the explanation of the plan to the men of war: that they should attack Ai, and when the men of Ai come out to fight, the army of the children of Israel withdraws before them, as the children of Israel withdrew from the first attack, noting the difference that in the first case they were defeated, whereas in the second case they pretend to be defeated in order to draw the army of Ai out of their city.

8.4.0.en: The men of Ai will be deceived and pursue the army of the children of Israel withdrawing before them, and will think that they are defeating them for the second time.

8.5.0.en: After the men of Ai have come out of it to pursue the army of the children of Israel, the ambush hidden behind Ai moves, enters the city and possesses it.

8.6.0.en: After the ambush of the children of Israel possesses the city of Ai, they burn it with fire, and by this they will have destroyed the evil and the wicked who are in the city.

8.6.1.en: If the devil fights us with many tricks, let us be confident that God is able to defeat him and guide us how to triumph over him.

8.6.2.en: We need only to obey God's commandments and the teachings of the Church.

8.6.3.en: (2) Carrying out the war plan (vv. 9-17:) 9 Joshua therefore sent them forth: and they went to lie in ambush, and abode between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of Ai: but Joshua lodged that night among the people. 10 And Joshua rose up early in the morning, and numbered the people, and went up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai. 11 And all the people, even the people of war that were with him, went up, and drew nigh, and came before the city, and pitched on the north side of Ai: now there was a valley between them and Ai. 12 And he took about five thousand men, and set them to lie in ambush between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city. 13 And when they had set the people, even all the host that was on the north of the city, and their liers in wait on the west of the city, Joshua went that night into the midst of the valley. 14 And it came to pass, when the king of Ai saw it, that they hasted and rose up early, and the men of the city went out against Israel to battle, he and all his people, at a time appointed, before the plain; but he wist not that there were liers in ambush against him behind the city. 15 And Joshua and all Israel made as if they were beaten before them, and fled by the way of the wilderness. 16 And all the people that were in Ai were called together to pursue after them: and they pursued after Joshua, and were drawn away from the city. 17 And there was not a man left in Ai or Bethel, that went not out after Israel: and they left the city open, and pursued after Israel.

8.7.0.en: The city of Ai was located southeast of Bethel, with rocky heights behind it, so the ambush of the children of Israel went by night and hid behind these heights west of Ai as Joshua had commanded them, while Joshua remained with the people and lodged among them that night (Map 2).

8.8.0.en: They had set: he means Joshua and the commanders of the army.

8.8.1.en: After Joshua sent the ambush at the beginning of the night to lie in wait west of Ai, he rose early before the dawn, that is, at the end of the night, and numbered his soldiers and moved with them toward Ai, which was located on a hill and could detect any military movements heading toward it in the daytime, and he reached the north of Ai with a valley separating him from it, while the ambush was hidden west of Ai between it and Bethel to attack Ai when Joshua commanded them. Then Joshua moved into the valley separating his forces from the city of Ai to inspect the place, and perhaps he withdrew to pray, asking God's help before the dawn and the attack on Ai.

8.9.0.en: At a time appointed: the suitable time that the king of Ai set, and most likely it is the time at which he had defeated the children of Israel the previous time. It may also be the time that Joshua set for carrying out his plan, and this shows the providence of God, who caused the king of Ai to come out to be defeated at the hands of the children of Israel.

8.9.1.en: At daybreak the king of Ai saw the armies of the children of Israel had come to attack him for the second time, so he gathered his army and went out with pride, confident of his victory over them as in the first time, and because of his pride he did not think that there might be an ambush against his city.

8.10.0.en: Made as if they were beaten: they pretended fear and flight.

8.10.1.en: Were called together: the king of Ai commanded his men to pursue the children of Israel.

8.10.2.en: They left the city open: that is, without guard, and therefore it is easy for the ambush to attack it.

8.10.3.en: The army of the children of Israel, under the leadership of Joshua, pretended fear of the army of Ai and fled before them by the way of the wilderness, and then the king of Ai commanded his armies to pursue the army of the children of Israel, so all the soldiers of Ai went out with pride, pursuing the children of Israel. The army of Bethel, which hurried to help the army of Ai, joined them, and all of them pursued the army of the children of Israel and left the city of Ai open and unguarded.

8.10.4.en: Pride made the king of Ai pursue the children of Israel and not guard against the possibility of an ambush. So be always humble, and God will reveal to you the devil's tricks and you will be able to overcome him. Be humble in your prayer before God and humble also in all your dealings with others, and you will secure your peace and your victory over Satan.

8.10.5.en: (3) The victory over Ai (vv. 18-29:) 18 And the Lord said unto Joshua, Stretch out the spear that is in thy hand toward Ai; for I will give it into thine hand. And Joshua stretched out the spear that he had in his hand toward the city. 19 And the ambush arose quickly out of their place, and they ran as soon as he had stretched out his hand: and they entered into the city, and took it, and hasted and set the city on fire. 20 And when the men of Ai looked behind them, they saw, and, behold, the smoke of the city ascended up to heaven, and they had no power to flee this way or that way: and the people that fled to the wilderness turned back upon the pursuers. 21 And when Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city, and that the smoke of the city ascended, then they turned again, and slew the men of Ai. 22 And the other issued out of the city against them; so they were in the midst of Israel, some on this side, and some on that side: and they smote them, so that they let none of them remain or escape. 23 And the king of Ai they took alive, and brought him to Joshua. 24 And it came to pass, when Israel had made an end of slaying all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness wherein they chased them, and when they were all fallen on the edge of the sword, until they were consumed, that all the Israelites returned unto Ai, and smote it with the edge of the sword. 25 And so it was, that all that fell that day, both of men and women, were twelve thousand, even all the men of Ai. 26 For Joshua drew not his hand back, wherewith he stretched out the spear, until he had utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai. 27 Only the cattle and the spoil of that city Israel took for a prey unto themselves, according unto the word of the Lord which he commanded Joshua. 28 And Joshua burnt Ai, and made it an heap for ever, even a desolation unto this day. 29 And the king of Ai he hanged on a tree until eventide: and as soon as the sun was down, Joshua commanded that they should take his carcase down from the tree, and cast it at the entering of the gate of the city, and raise thereon a great heap of stones, that remaineth unto this day.

8.11.1.en: God is the commander of the army of His people in war, for after all the soldiers of Ai and Bethel had gone out, God commanded Joshua to raise the spear toward Ai, and the soldiers hidden in the ambush saw it, and then they hurried and seized the city of Ai and burned it, and the flames rose to heaven, so as to frighten the soldiers of Ai and make it easy to defeat them.

8.12.2.en: The soldiers of Ai were surprised by smoke filling the air, and they turned behind them to find their city burning, and they were alarmed and bewildered, and while they were alarmed, the soldiers of the children of Israel who were pretending to flee before the soldiers of Ai turned around and attacked the soldiers of Ai, and the soldiers of the ambush also attacked the soldiers of Ai and the soldiers of Bethel, so that they were surrounded between the soldiers of the children of Israel, and they killed them all and none escaped.

8.13.0.en: Since the soldiers of Ai were alarmed, it became easy for the soldiers of the children of Israel to seize their king and hand him over to Joshua, and this increased their alarm and despair, which helped the soldiers of Israel to kill the soldiers of Ai. Then they entered the city of Ai and killed all who were in it, women, old people and children, as the Lord commanded, to remove evil.

8.13.1.en: The number of persons killed in Ai was twelve thousand, and the dead of Bethel were not mentioned because the emphasis was on the victory over Ai. Joshua may have taken Bethel at this time or afterward, but in any case he took it among the cities in Canaan (ch. 12:16). Joshua kept the spear raised throughout the battle, as Moses raised his hands like a cross in the victory over Amalek (Ex 17), and this was by God's command so that the eyes of the warriors would remain on the spear, which signifies the cross, and they would be united together and so achieve a complete victory.

8.14.0.en: The children of Israel took the spoil of the city for themselves, according to God's word to Joshua, and had Achan waited he would have taken many things and not lost his life and possessions (ch. 7).

8.15.0.en: Joshua completed the burning of all of Ai, and it became a heap of rubble and was turned from a city of importance into a mound, and by this he removed the evil and uncleanness that had filled the place.

8.16.0.en: They hanged the king of Ai on a tree, which was a means of killing the worst offenders and an example of shame and disgrace, and at evening they took his body down as the Law prescribes (Deut 21:23) and cast it at the gate of the city and raised over it a heap of stones, so that everyone who sees the heap or the mound of the city knows the end of evil and the wicked.

8.16.1.en: If God is the leader of your life, be confident that you are able to triumph in all the wars of the demons; He will guide you and support you, and do not be alarmed at all their movements and tricks, because your God is with you. Hold fast to Him and seek Him, and He will always lead your life.

8.16.2.en: (4) The blessing and the curse (vv. 30-35:) 30 Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal, 31 As Moses the servant of the Lord commanded the children of Israel, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses, an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron: and they offered thereon burnt offerings unto the Lord, and sacrificed peace offerings. 32 And he wrote there upon the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the children of Israel. 33 And all Israel, and their elders, and officers, and their judges, stood on this side the ark and on that side before the priests the Levites, which bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord, as well the stranger, as he that was born among them; half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal; as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded before, that they should bless the people of Israel. 34 And afterward he read all the words of the law, the blessings and cursings, according to all that is written in the book of the law. 35 There was not a word of all that Moses commanded, which Joshua read not before all the congregation of Israel, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them.

8.17.0.en: Mount Ebal: a mountain located north of Shechem (present-day Nablus), on which six tribes stood to proclaim the curse of those who violate the Law and the divine commandments (Map 2). Whole stones: sound stones with even faces, prepared.

8.17.1.en: After that victory Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal according to the conditions Moses had taught him (Deut 27:5), that the altar be built of sound stones and that no chisel be lifted upon it while they were building it, out of care not to resemble the altars of idols on which their images and statues were engraved. They offered to the Lord burnt offerings and peace offerings of thanksgiving, and he built the altar on Mount Ebal, on which the divine curses were recited upon whoever disobeys God (Deut 27:11-26), to confirm the uprightness of the people of God and their keeping away from these curses and their obedience to His commands, which led to their victory over Ai.

8.18.0.en: They set up pillars of stone and coated them with lime or some similar material to make it easy to write on them, and then they wrote on them the commandments and the Law.

8.19.0.en: Officers: leaders of the people who understand the Law, and they are deputies of the elders.

8.19.1.en: Moses had commanded his people that if they entered the Promised Land they should set up an altar to the Lord and offer thank offerings and write a copy of the Law on stone pillars for the people to read and remember, and proclaim the blessings of God upon whoever obeys Him and His curses upon whoever disobeys Him, on Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal (Deut 27:11-26). So Joshua carried out all that Moses commanded, and the priests bore the ark, and the elders of the people and their officers and judges stood around the ark on the right and on the left, and with them the people, who were in two parts, six tribes at Mount Gerizim and six tribes at Mount Ebal, and all the Jews stood, both the native-born and the strangers who joined them and became Jews, because God is the God of the whole world, who desires the salvation of all through faith.

8.20.0.en: After the proclamation of the blessing and the curse and the ratification of them by both parties, Joshua completed the reading of the commandments of the Lord and the Law which He had delivered to Moses, before all the people, and explained it (Deut 31:12).

8.20.1.en: May you read the Holy Bible every day, and also repeat some of its verses that you choose, to keep your mind and heart pure throughout your day and so that you do not turn aside from them into any sin, and you will receive the abundant blessings of God in your life. The trick of the Gibeonites
